absent: Full layouts of address space, area, folio, page, page table entry, gather, soft leaf, policy, and walk structures beyond fields touched here
Semantics of batch, modify, flush, lazy MMU, NUMA eligibility, normal page resolution, and writability predicate helpers
Userfault marker creation and query helpers and read write protect area test details
Page range walk implementation with huge and middle directory handlers and read versus write walk lock semantics
Policy object lifecycle and helpers for creation, duplication, comparison, reference counting, nodemask validation, and area policy lookup
Migration helpers for isolating, moving, allocating targets, writeback, and least recently used cache control, plus huge pool allocation
VMA modification machinery with iterators, locking assertions, split logic, and driver policy hooks
Numeric values of error codes and architecture specific page table bit layouts
Concurrency, lifetime, and ordering guarantees beyond the locks explicitly shown

findings.text: VMA policy modification helper is globally visible. It accepts an iterator with predecessor and target area plus an address interval and a new policy, packages those into a modify request state, delegates to the generic VMA modification routine, and returns the resulting area pointer.

Cross node page migration driver is globally visible with two build alternatives. One alternative iterates over source node masks and migrates pages toward destination nodes with accounting of failures. The other alternative always reports unimplemented, indicating the feature can be compiled out.

Small page protection changes operate one page middle directory slice at a time. The routine announces small page size to the gather structure, maps the page table under its spinlock with a retry error when mapping fails, drains pending batched invalidations, enables lazy MMU mode for the loop, advances by a variable batch size until the end, counts changed pages, disables lazy mode, then unmaps and unlocks using the final slot.

Desired state filtering avoids redundant work. Missing or non large folios force a batch of one, while large folios delegate to a flagged batch helper. NUMA hinting skips entries already without access. Read write protect tracking skips only entries already carrying both no access and its marker, while plain no access entries are still promoted. NUMA eligibility is checked per folio with single threaded private knowledge, and ineligible runs are skipped using an unflagged batch probe. Eligible present runs use a flagged batch probe that respects soft dirty and write state, limited by remaining pages, with single page and multi page commit paths.

Present entry update follows start then modify then commit. The start snapshot is transformed to the new protection, userfault write or read write protection sets its marker while resolve variants clear it, and areas with read write protect semantics restore PAGE_NONE when the marker remains so trapping continues. A writable promotion attempt may set write, otherwise a plain commit occurs. Commit advances position and frame numbers by index within the batch, optionally marks writable, publishes the entries, and flushes translation entries only when the old to new transition requires it.

Non present non empty entries are treated as soft leaves. Write capable migration entries become readable, with an exclusive variant for anonymous folios and a shared variant otherwise, preserving soft dirty where shown. Write capable device private entries become readable without preserving soft dirty but preserving any userfault marker. Poison and guard markers are left untouched. When userfault resolve is requested, its marker entries are cleared to empty and counted as changed, otherwise markers are left alone. Userfault protection sets its swap marker while resolve clears it, and the table is updated only when the new value differs.

Empty entries are ignored except for userfault write protection. When that mode is active and the area uses markers, file backed coverage installs a dedicated write protection marker for empty slots and counts each installation, so later faults can trap despite the absence of a present mapping.

Writable promotion diverges by sharing distinguished with VMA_SHARED_BIT. Shared areas consult a shared writability predicate and commit the whole batch with the resulting decision. Private areas require both a private writability predicate and an anonymous folio, otherwise they commit without write. When both hold, the batch is split into maximal runs sharing the same anonymous exclusive flag value, and each run is committed with write set exactly for exclusive runs.

Page table exclusion for the range walk is provided by the per table spinlock acquired during mapping and released after the loop, with the unmap call anchored on the last visited slot. Translation invalidation batching is coordinated by draining pending work before entering lazy MMU mode and leaving that mode after the loop. Upper level preparation is a macro that only when population is needed attempts lower table allocation and reports out of memory on failure.

Policy and migration walks use distinct exclusion levels. Range queueing selects a read walk lock normally and a write walk lock when flag MPOL_MF_WRLOCK is present. Full space migration and address policy lookup hold the address space read lock while locating areas, dropping it before operations that may sleep. Policy replacement asserts write exclusion on the area and publishes the pointer under address space protection. Current task policy nodemask reads and updates are serialized by the task lock.

Range queueing state carries a destination list with control flags plus a node mask pointer, the original start and end, a first area pointer initially empty, and a failure count. Two operation tables share the same huge entry and middle directory entry and test callbacks but differ in walk lock mode, one PGWALK_RDLOCK and one PGWALK_WRLOCK, allowing the same traversal logic under different exclusion.

Single source migration control targets one destination node with allocation flags GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE and __GFP_THISNODE and reason MR_SYSCALL. Policy replacement state duplicates the incoming policy, optionally offers it to the area driver hook with cleanup on hook failure, then publishes the duplicate while releasing the old policy.

Range queue validation enforces containment and continuity. It asserts the walked interval lies within the current area, records the first area, and rejects gaps at head middle or tail with a fault error unless discontiguity is explicitly allowed. Non migratable areas are skipped without scanning unless strict checking is requested. Scanning proceeds only when strict or move style flags are present, otherwise the area is skipped. A walk that never meets an area reports a fault for a wholly empty range, otherwise the result is the failure count.

Bind range update clamps the end to the current area end and chooses the start as the requested start when inside the area or the area start otherwise. When the existing area policy already equals the new policy the routine returns success without changes. Otherwise it splits or modifies the area over the clamped interval to carry the new policy and then replaces the stored policy object.

Task policy setting allocates a scratch mask, creates a new policy object, validates its node mask under the task lock with cleanup on failure, publishes it as the current policy, and resets interleave cursor state for interleave style modes. Task policy query rejects unknown flags, handles allowed set queries exclusively, looks up the area for address queries with fault on miss and defaults when no policy applies, resolves node queries by direct page lookup for address mode or by interleave cursor with a weighted variant, masks internal mode flags before exposing, and prefers a stored user mask when present.

Multi node migration disables the least recently used cache across the whole operation. It copies the source mask and repeatedly picks a source and remapped destination pair, skipping sources that also appear in the destination when source and destination weights differ, skipping pairs that map to themselves, memorizing the latest moving pair and preferring a destination no longer remaining as a source. Each chosen source is cleared and migrated alone, accumulating positive per source failure counts and aborting on negative error, with the final count capped at INT_MAX.

Policy based migration target allocation adjusts the interleave index by the folio index shifted by its order. Huge table folios resolve a node mask and node through the policy helper and allocate from the huge pool with fallback allowance for reason MR_MEMPOLICY_MBIND. Other folios use GFP_TRANSHUGE for large folios and GFP_HIGHUSER_MOVABLE with __GFP_RETRY_MAYFAIL and __GFP_COMP otherwise, then delegate to the policy folio allocator with flags plus order plus policy plus index plus local node, while the alternate build always yields no folio.

Range migration exposes a layered entry structure. A range queue helper builds the queue state, selects read or write walk operations from flags, runs the page range walk, maps an untouched walk to a fault, and otherwise returns queued failures. A single source helper isolates the whole user space with discontiguity tolerance under read lock, migrates the isolated list synchronously with putback on error, and adds isolation failures. The global driver loops the single source helper over computed pairs.

Failure modes are explicit. Table mapping failure reports EAGAIN to request a retry. Lower table and scratch allocation failures report ENOMEM. Holes and missing areas report EFAULT. Invalid flag combinations and address use without address mode report EINVAL. Disabled migration reports ENOSYS. Unknown policy modes hit a fatal check. Error and guard markers are deliberately left unchanged so future access still faults.

Protection change control uses distinct flag facts. Flags MM_CP_PROT_NUMA and MM_CP_UFFD_WP and MM_CP_UFFD_RWP plus resolve variants MM_CP_UFFD_WP_RESOLVE and MM_CP_UFFD_RWP_RESOLVE plus MM_CP_TRY_CHANGE_WRITABLE steer filtering and marker handling. Batch probing distinguishes an unflagged skip probe from a flagged probe using FPB_RESPECT_SOFT_DIRTY and FPB_RESPECT_WRITE. Marker PTE_MARKER_UFFD_WP identifies protected empty entries.

Memory policy control uses mode and flag facts. Modes MPOL_BIND and MPOL_INTERLEAVE and MPOL_PREFERRED and MPOL_PREFERRED_MANY and MPOL_WEIGHTED_INTERLEAVE and MPOL_LOCAL and MPOL_DEFAULT with a subset MPOL_MODE_FLAGS exposable to user space. Query flags MPOL_F_NODE and MPOL_F_ADDR and MPOL_F_MEMS_ALLOWED distinguish requests. Queue and migrate flags MPOL_MF_DISCONTIG_OK and MPOL_MF_STRICT and MPOL_MF_MOVE and MPOL_MF_MOVE_ALL and MPOL_MF_WRLOCK distinguish tolerance and checking and movement and locking.
